subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a substantial, robust module for an alebrije design: a jaguar-bodied, eagle-headed creature with wings, rendered in vivid Oaxacan-style carved wood aesthetics with bold colors and dot patterns.

For the skeleton I'm sketching a spine chain from hips through chest to a raised eagle-like neck and hooked-beak head, a curling flame-tipped tail, four digitigrade-style legs with IK, and wings mounted at the shoulders extended outward in a rest T-pose, built from a jointed wing chain with roughly nine painted feather shapes attached along it.

Working out feather geometry...

Writing feather paint logic...

Writing the alebrije skin paint function...

Defining spine and neck curves for the torso sweep, shaping hips, chest, and neck proportions like a jaguar's build.

Still defining the skeleton hierarchy...

For the body geometry, I'm sweeping tubes along the spine and neck chains separately, matching their radii at the junction so the chest tapers smoothly into the thinner neck base.

I'm planning a piecewise-linear radius function across the body so hips, waist, chest, and neck transition thickness naturally, then moving on to the head structure—an eagle skull with a beak attached at the end of the neck.

For the beak, I'm sketching a hooked, laterally compressed sweep following a curved path from forehead forward and down, tapering the radius toward the tip, using local coordinates relative to the head's forward orientation.

Now I'm planning a separate jaw joint, attached as a child of the head, to handle the lower beak independently.

For the beak itself, I'm thinking yellow-orange painted wood with a dark tip outline, building the lower beak as a rigid sweep bound to the jaw bone and the upper beak fixed to the skull. For the eyes, I'm planning large decal textures on a sphere-shaped skull part, placing the eye artwork with the skin surface for proper positioning.

I'm adding a crest of five big colorful feathers fanning above the head like an alebrije headdress, plus small round jaguar ears with painted inner discs on the skull sides for that hybrid cue. Now I'm sketching the thick jaguar legs with toed paws, positioning the front limb from shoulder down to foot.

Calculating leg segment lengths...

Front legs get names shoulder/elbow/wrist, hind legs hip/knee/hock/ankle, matching joint count plus tip. I'll sweep the limb chains directly as tubes for smooth joint skinning, tapering thigh radius from thick to thin toward the foot.

For paws I'm modeling a rounded ellipsoid foot (radii roughly 0.075, 0.05, 0.1) positioned so its bottom sits at ground level y=0, plus small toe cones with tiny dark claw tips attached at the chain's tip joint.

Now I'm planning the wing structure: anchoring shoulders on the back above the body, then chaining out through elbow, wrist, and tip joints that spread outward, upward, and slightly back to give a natural wing silhouette.

I'm working out feather placement along the wing spar, with secondary feathers rooted along the shoulder-to-wrist span fanning backward and outward, and primaries extending from the wrist to the hand tip.

I'll bind each feather to its joint bone, then layer a covert row of shorter rounded feathers over the primaries and secondaries with slight height offsets to avoid z-fighting—roughly 60 small extrusions per wing total, which should still be cheap to render.

I'm working out the feather geometry parameters now: small bevel with thin capped thickness for a clean tip, and computing the perpendicular axis via cross product to orient each feather correctly along its direction vector.

I'll stack feather rows with slight y-offsets (coverts over secondaries over primaries) to avoid z-fighting, and tilt each wing plane slightly for a natural slope before moving on to the tail geometry.

For the tail, I'm plotting a curved spine of points rising from the hips out and up like an eagle's tail, with shrinking radius toward the tip, then capping it with a fan of seven feathers radiating outward using angled extrusion directions.

For the neck, I'm blending jaguar spots into an eagle-like feathered ruff by scattering card feathers in a ring around the neck base, angling them outward and downward to simulate layered plumage.

For the ring, flow should flatten onto the plane so feathers droop down and back like hackles, and I'll use cross:true so they're visible from all sides. Now I'm sizing the eagle head: skull as a scaled sphere at the neck's end, oriented forward and slightly down to match the neck's upward curve.

Defining neck joint positions...

Writing beak coloring logic...

Adding nostril spheres stuck to the beak surface at slight angles on either side. Then I'm planning brow ridges as colored tube sweeps arcing over each eye, computing eye positions from the skull center and radius on the head bone.

Computing eye placement using spherical coordinates on the skull sphere, landing around forward 0.1, up 0.05, left 0.077, then adjusting the brow endpoints to sit just above the eye's top edge. Next I'm planning the head crest as five fanning extrusions at the back of the skull in the sagittal plane.

Working out the orientation math so each feather stands upright, thin sideways, with the extrusion direction following the crest curve and thickness running along the lateral axis.

Working out the orthogonalization so plane normal N stays perpendicular to feather direction d, then setting up the crest with seven feathers fanned across angles, computing each one's direction and normal using cross products against the z-axis.

I'll go with a coronal crest orientation, N roughly [0,0.3,1] normalized, so the feather fan reads boldly like a headdress from the front while staying coherent from 3/4 and side angles. I'm drafting a feather helper function that takes an origin, direction, length, width, normal, bone reference, and color palette to paint each plume.

Writing feather paint function...

Refining the width profile...

Writing jaguar skin shader...

Adding shading toward the belly, then working on a dorsal zigzag stripe pattern using alternating colors based on position along the body to create a triangular scale effect.

For the neck, I'm thinking of using a feathered scale pattern blending cream, yellow, and pink tones with dark edges, giving it an eagle-ruff feel that transitions into the jaguar pattern below.

For the head, I'm planning a cream base with small dotted clusters scattered across it, using a custom dot-grid paint function, while keeping the eye decal area readable with its own ink-outlined details. Legs would carry a different jaguar rosette variation.

For the legs, I'm thinking stripes of orange banded with magenta and turquoise rings, with the paws getting a separate painted treatment—maybe keeping the jaguar rosette pattern consistent down the legs rather than complicating things with a different paw color scheme. I'm also considering giving the front paws eagle talons to lean into the jaguar-eagle hybrid concept.

I'm deciding to scale back given time constraints—keeping jaguar-style paws throughout but painting the claws a golden color for visual interest. Each paw will have three toe spheres and three claw cones attached at the bone tip joint, built through a helper function. I'm also planning decorative touches like dot rows and alebrije-style flower motifs on the shoulders and haunches.

For the decals, I'm placing a flower emblem (magenta petals, yellow center, with leaves and dot accents) on each flank and a sun/spiral greca pattern on the haunches, projected onto the body surface using the decal system with position and direction parameters.

Since legs aren't part of the body sweep, I'll set the center explicitly rather than relying on bbox default, and skip mirroring the decals since they're already symmetric-ish. For the wing structure, I'm naming the joint chain root/elbow/wrist/tip with a "wing" role, then sweeping the arm with a solid turquoise feathered color.

Now I'm working out joint hierarchy: hips as root, with spine, tail, and hind legs all parenting off hips, while front legs, wings, and neck attach near the chest joint further up the spine. I'm placing the chest joint at the last spine segment and starting the neck from that same point.

Setting up the sweep function to generate the body mesh along the spine chain...

Now I'm working out the tail: a short chain parented to the hips, positioned at the rear, with a sweep that tapers and gets painted with alternating colored stripe rings.

At the very tip I'm adding a fan of feathers, orienting them using the tail's final heading so they splay outward in a roughly horizontal plane.

Checking the wings now, extending them further for a more dramatic span, with the arm bending up through elbow and wrist to form a raised V-shape ending in sharp primary tips.

I'll use wing.at(t) consistently for both position and bone lookup, converting the point to a vector via the helper. For the fan angles, I'm mapping primaries from 30° to 85° increasing toward the tip, and secondaries from a narrower 5° to 20° range, with coverts following the underlying position blend.

I'm setting feather lengths and widths for each type — primaries longest in the middle, shorter secondaries and coverts — and mirroring the x-direction with a sign factor for symmetric wing sides. Now I'm defining color palette arrays for each feather type, assigning base, mid, and tip colors plus a constant cream dot color, alternating the primary palette by index.

I'm sketching out the set of decorative texture SVGs I'll need: an eye motif, a flower for the flank, a spiral/sun for the haunch, an inner-ear circle, a couple of colorful ruff feather cards, and a sun-face emblem for the chest — skipping extras like a forehead mark or pedestal. Writing eye SVG code...

Building the iris with orange outer ring and yellow inner circle, plus a black pupil and white highlights, then a thick lid stroke and a magenta eyeliner flick. I want to center the pupil around cx=50 to keep the eye symmetrical regardless of mirroring, with the brow flick placed at the outer corner.

For the raptor eye I'm shaping an almond path where the brow slopes down toward the beak, so the outer corner sits high and the inner corner droops low. Now moving on to the flower, where I'll build petals from rotated ellipses.

Writing SVG code...

Now I'm planning additional decorative motifs: a sun emblem with alternating triangular rays and concentric dotted rings for the haunch, plus feather-textured leaf cards with rib detailing in two color palettes, to place alongside the flower emblem across shoulders, chest, and flanks.

For the ears, I'm going simple -- a larger orange sphere with a smaller pink sphere pushed forward as the flat inner ear, no texture needed. I'm positioning them on the head slightly forward and up, making sure they don't clash with the back-angled crest placement.

Checking for collisions now: the crest feathers fan out at wide angles from the center, and I need to verify their roots don't overlap the ear position. Adjusting the ears lower and more to the side with a smaller radius should keep things clean, even if they end up half-embedded in the skull, and narrowing the crest fan angle avoids any real intersection.

Now I'm working out where the chest decal would go, but since the neck geometry covers that region near the front, I'll skip the chest sun decal and rely on a feather ruff around the neck base instead. I'm tracing where the body ends and the neck's rounded cap extends forward to figure out the exact junction point.

Checking proportions: overall jaguar length from hips to chest works out to about 1.35m plus tail, shoulder height around 0.8, with paw placements set for front and hind legs. I'm now sketching the front leg geometry -- shoulder to foot positions and segment lengths -- to make sure the limb reads as nearly straight with a slight bend at the elbow.

For the limb chains, I'm confirming the polyline array of points works directly as path input, with one joint per span between points, and sweeping a smooth skin over it to round the corners naturally. Then I'm adding paw parts as scaled sphere geometry attached near the foot bone to form the toes.

Adding toe spheres and claw spikes...

I'm thinking through smaller details now—pupils, nostrils, maybe skipping the mouth gape since it's not essential. For the beak I'm mapping color along the sweep path, and I'm considering adding a small glowing amber gem between the brows as a decorative forehead accent.

Writing the import statements...

Still defining colors and helper functions...

Adding ring colors, then blending in a cream belly with small blue dots and a dorsal zigzag stripe for shading.

For the head I'm reconsidering a cream base paint with turquoise or magenta dot patches near the top for cheek detail, keeping dots subtle so they don't clutter the eye decals. The body and legs share the same cell pattern and seed for continuity, the wing arm gets a turquoise/yellow dot treatment, and now I'm working out the beak paint with a threshold-based color split.

For the beak I'm settling on a golden base with magenta stripe bands using a modulo pattern, an orange tip cap near the base, and an ink-dark tip at the very end, keeping the lower beak paint matching. For the ear I'm thinking orange with a pink inner section, possibly reusing the jaguar-pattern paint for the outer ear to keep the motif consistent.

Now I'm starting the main build function, setting up the skeleton with a hips joint and a spine chain built from catmull-rom spline points, then sweeping a body mesh profile along that spine...

Writing neck chain and sweep...

Building the skull as a scaled sphere attached to the head joint, checking that the world-axis scaling for width, height, and length lines up correctly without extra rotation.

I'm adding a small throat puff sphere beneath the skull to blend the neck-head junction, then starting the beak as a swept bezier curve with a tapering cross-section profile.

Writing beak sweep code...

Now setting up the jaw joint and swept path to form the lower beak, tapering it to match the upper beak's proportions.

I'm adding a small red tongue sphere nestled in the jaw, then checking that the upper and lower beak surfaces meet cleanly at the closed position. For the nostrils, I'm embedding tiny spheres on the upper beak surface at symmetric angles along the beak's local coordinate frame.

For the eyes, I'm computing hit points on the skull surface by sweeping around a center point at mirrored azimuth angles, then placing eye decals there sized and oriented to the surface normal, mirroring the left/right pair.

I'm checking whether the decal inherits bone weighting automatically from the landing point, then considering tweaking eye size slightly smaller since 0.1 feels too large relative to skull radius. Now I'm adding brow capsules positioned symmetrically on either side of the head using mirrored x-offsets.

Working through the geometry, I'm verifying the brow ridges stay roughly on the skull surface by calculating the sphere's radius at different heights and depths, confirming the placement is close enough even if the scaled skull shape makes it approximate. Now I'm moving on to defining the ears.

Adding inner ear details...

Now I'm setting up the crest feathers, spacing seven of them radially from a root point with angles from -48 to 48 degrees, varying their lengths so the center feather is longest and tapering outward.

Writing feather helper function...

Defining the width profile function for the feather shape, checking continuity at the midpoint and tracing sample outline points down to the tip to confirm it tapers smoothly to a sharp point, then moving on to write the paint function.

Defining color bands and wing geometry...

I'm tapering the wing's radius thicker near the shoulder for a sleeve-like ruff, then setting up feather points that sample position and bone from the wing curve. Now I'm working out the primary feather spacing and angles so the outermost tip feather points outward correctly.

Still working out covert feather spacing and widths relative to arm length, plus slight y-offsets to make layered feathers sit naturally, and I'm starting to define color palette sets for each feather group.

Assigning alternating color triples to primaries, secondaries, and coverts, keeping the palette compact, and confirming wing mirroring works correctly through the sign flip. I'm tallying up the total feather count per wing and rough triangle counts for the extruded outlines to keep things performant.

Now I'm working out the tail feather geometry: positioning a chain of tail points sweeping back and up, then fanning out seven feathers at 18-degree intervals with normalized direction vectors and tapering lengths.

For coloring, I'm writing a paint function that slices the tail into fourteen segments, inserting ink outlines at segment boundaries and cycling through magenta, yellow, turquoise, and orange bands across the rest.

Now I'm moving on to the legs, defining front leg root and foot positions and building a limb chain between them, thinking through how to specify bend directions per joint.

I'm setting up the leg chain with named joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist) parented to the spine, then sweeping it with a tapered radius and adding a shoulder blob sphere for extra bulk at the joint.

Now I'm defining a paw helper and working out the hind leg chain, with root/knee/hock/foot points bending via alternating directions so the knee and hock form the inner joints.

I'm adding a decal onto the thigh sphere, checking that the haunch placement stays within the body's bounding proportions, and planning a similar shoulder blob with a flower decal for the front leg.

Now I'm setting up the hind leg's chain of joints and building a paw helper that adds a palm sphere plus toe spheres at offset positions along the foot.

Next I'm adding claw spikes angled downward from each toe tip, checking they clear the floor plane, then starting on ruff feather cards placed around the neck at varying radii and sizes...

Checking the flow projection per ring side confirms it mostly points downward/backward, giving a natural droop to the cards. I'm deciding against the cross (double-sided) geometry to keep things cheap, though I need to double check that card faces don't look edge-on from the front viewing angle.

I'm skipping extra elements like a mane band, but adding a small glowing forehead gem near the beak base as a signature detail.

Now I'm adding decal ideas—flower shapes on the shoulder blobs and a sun motif on the haunches—while confirming the ground contact points and symmetry all check out. I'm starting to write a helper function to generate flower SVG petals.

Writing SVG petal code...

Now sketching the sun icon with rotating triangular rays and a layered disc, then starting on the feather card shape with a curved teardrop outline...

Adding a vertical gradient along the feather from base to tip with an ink outline...

Now I'm checking build order -- joints need to exist before chains reference them, legs parent off spine joints, and neck spans three joints. I also need the body sweep finished before placing ear and flank decals, since those rely on sampling the surface of the completed body mesh.

I'm sizing the flank flower decal to fit within the body's half-height, separating it from the shoulder blob by z-position so they don't overlap, and leaving world-up as the default decal orientation. Checking the total part count stays under the target range while keeping quality reasonably high.

Now I'm adding finer surface details—a chest loop sweep of beaded studs around the girth at a spine joint, computing the perpendicular loop plane at that point and sweeping a thin colored ring with beads distributed along it.

The tangent shift is negligible so sphere beads work fine using b.part with the at point. For the hip belt, I should avoid the root joint since its axis points up and would make the loop horizontal—better to use spine.joints[1] near the waist for a proper girth band with turquoise beads.

I'll create two swept bands, one at the waist joint and one at the chest joint, using closed loop paths with small radius sweeps to get painted band effects. The loop function should accept a Joint directly based on the docs, and sweep carries the loop weights fine for closed paths. I'll also add small details like a tail tuft and wing spots, plus a tiny sphere geometry helper for the ears.

Writing imports...

Still defining interpolation helper...

Now I'm working out torso keyframes along the spine chain for thickness variation, plus hip widening near the rear, and setting up the crest root position and directional vector for feather placement.

For the jaw, I'm considering adding a slight 8-degree open pose for readability, posing the forward-pointing bone to tilt down even though it's applied after the lower beak mesh is built.

Writing wing and feather helper code...
